# masque

> Synthetic copies of confidential data tables, for writing analysis
> code without the real data.

`masque` makes a synthetic copy of a confidential table. Analysts write
and test code on the copy without seeing the real values. The data owner
then runs the finished code on the real data, using a private recipe
that maps the codes in the copy back to the real labels.

By default, every outcome and covariate is simulated independently, with
no link to other columns or to the real rows. Each numeric column keeps
only an eleven-point summary: its 1st percentile, deciles and 99th
percentile. The experimental design and the pattern of missing values
are kept exactly, and category labels are replaced by codes. When the
code needs correlations between columns, use `mode = "collaborate"`, or
`mode = "local"` if the copy will not leave the data owner. Treatment
effects can also be mimicked by setting `conditional = TRUE`. Each step
discloses more about the real data, and masque gives no formal privacy
guarantee.

It is for owners of confidential research data who want an outside
analyst to build the analysis without seeing the real values, and for
the analysts who build it. The input can be a single table, a folder of
files or a multi-sheet workbook.

The [changelog](https://max578.github.io/masque/news/index.html) lists
what changed in each release.

Every table masque returns is a `data.table`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Installation

Pre-built binaries from r-universe:

``` r

install.packages(
  "masque",
  repos = c("https://max578.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org")
)
```

Or from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("max578/masque")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Two-minute example

``` r

library(masque)

# Read a small public fixture (alpha-design field trial; John & Williams, 1995).
f  <- system.file("extdata", "john_alpha.csv", package = "masque")
df <- read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = TRUE)

# One guided call: read -> propose roles -> (review) -> mask -> audit.
# In an interactive session it pauses to let you review the plan;
# ask = FALSE skips the pause. The default copy keeps the design and the
# missing values; every other value is drawn independently.
m <- masque(df, seed = 1L)

synth <- synthetic(m)   # hand this to the analyst
rec   <- recipe(m)      # keep this private

# Analyst builds a pipeline against the synthetic namespace ...
fit <- lm(yield ~ gen + rep, data = synth)

# ... and the data owner re-targets it to the original data.
preds <- predict(fit, newdata = apply_recipe(df, rec))

# A description of the clone the analyst can plan with: sizes, roles and
# counts, never a value.
card <- data_card(m, name = "alpha_trial")
```

A folder of files or a multi-sheet workbook works the same way. Pass the
path to
[`masque()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/masque.md) and it
masks every table at once, aliasing shared keys consistently so the
synthetic tables still join.

If the table needs tidying first,
[`clean_table()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/clean_table.md)
makes column names valid and trims whitespace, and
[`conform_table()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/conform_table.md)
merges near-duplicate labels and sets column types, reporting each
change.

### Multi-environment trials

[`detect_design()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/detect_design.md)
recognises environment columns, such as site or year, and the design
within each environment. By default, and in collaborate mode, the
environment labels are replaced by codes and every row stays in its
environment. The clone does not keep genotype-by-environment effects, so
it is no substitute for the real data in scientific inference.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Known-truth controls

A pipeline developed on the clone can be checked against datasets in
which the answer is known. A control spec, declared once, names the
column to reassign, the design strata it is permuted within, the outcome
an effect is planted on and the size of that effect. From it,
[`controls()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/controls.md)
derives a null (every analysed column permuted), negative replicates
(one column permuted within strata) and positive replicates (the
negative plus the planted shift), by permutation alone. The same spec
runs on the clone for the analyst and, with a private seed, on the
original for the owner, who returns a verdict about the pipeline rather
than a dataset.

``` r

spec <- control_spec(on = "gen", target = "yield", effect = list(sd = 0.5),
                     strata = "rep", n = 19L, seed = 2026L)
ctl <- controls(synthetic(m), roles(m), spec)
control_table(ctl, "positive", 1L)
```

A
[`masque_plan()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/masque_plan.md)
holds the roles and the spec together, so the spec is fixed before any
real result exists. `mask(df, plan)` resolves it on the source,
[`handover()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/handover.md)
gives the analyst the clone and the plan in clone vocabulary, and
`controls(real, plan, recipe = rec)` runs it on the owner’s side.

## Threat model

`masque` gives no formal privacy guarantee such as differential privacy.
It makes copies for writing analysis code, with explicit confidentiality
safeguards. Read [Confidentiality and the threat
model](https://max578.github.io/masque/articles/confidentiality.html)
before using it.

**What `masque` does**

- Preserves enough structure for pipelines to run unchanged.
- Provides three modes.
  - `null`, the default, keeps the design and the missing values
    exactly. It draws each numeric value from its column’s 1st
    percentile, deciles and 99th percentile, and each categorical value
    uniformly over the column’s levels, which are renamed to codes.
  - `local` keeps the real structure (correlations, and real labels
    unless you code them). It keeps identifiers and free text and runs
    no audit, so its output is for the data owner only.
  - `collaborate` keeps the correlations, replaces treatment and
    category labels with codes (numeric treatment levels included), adds
    small random noise within each value’s measurement resolution, and
    runs the leakage audit.
- In the null and collaborate modes, columns that look like identifiers
  or free text are dropped. They are found by name (such as `id`,
  `email` or `farmer`) or by mostly distinct character values, so a
  numeric identifier with an ordinary name can pass: review the proposed
  roles. A column that would be resampled from a table of fewer than
  five rows is refused.
- The leakage audit compares the copy with the original, column by
  column and for the table as a whole. A HIGH finding raises a warning
  and blocks masque’s own writers until it is resolved or overridden.
- Synthesises a column that is constant within a trial or site once per
  unit, so the clone keeps one value per trial, and keeps linked event
  times in order (`events =`).
- Keeps treatment, block and environment means on request
  (`conditional = TRUE`, in local or collaborate mode). Treatment means
  on the clone then track those of the real data, and block and
  environment effects stay detectable. [What a conditional clone keeps
  of the
  design](https://max578.github.io/masque/articles/design_preservation.html)
  tests this on eight field designs.
- Records every translation (column names, factor levels) in a private
  `recipe`. The recipe holds the real labels, the original column names
  and the seed, so together with the synthetic it undoes every alias.
  Keep it with the original data and never send it with the synthetic.
- Audits its own output
  ([`audit_mask()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/audit_mask.md)),
  raises HIGH findings as classed warnings the guided flow never
  silences, and refuses package-managed writes while a HIGH finding
  stands (an explicit `allow_high = TRUE` override is available, warned
  and recorded in the recipe).

**What `masque` does not do**

- It is not a universal anonymiser, and it does not provide
  differential-privacy guarantees.
- It does not make outputs safe for public release.
- It does not anonymise rare strata, small designs, or operational
  metadata (small site-by-year combinations, contact names,
  geolocations).
- It does not certify compliance with any privacy, health, banking, or
  research-governance obligation. It can contribute evidence to such a
  decision; the decision itself is organisational and legal.
- It does not rewrite arbitrary pipeline source code.

**Bottom line.** Generating a synthetic table is not a release decision.
In the Five Safes framework for controlled data access, `masque`
contributes to *Safe Data* and *Safe Outputs*; Safe People, Safe
Projects, and Safe Settings are governance questions no package can
answer. The collaborate workflow assumes only the synthetic crosses the
trust boundary.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Related packages

- [synthpop](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=synthpop) makes
  synthetic versions of confidential microdata for release, synthesising
  one variable at a time from conditional models, and measures their
  utility and disclosure risk.
- [sdcMicro](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=sdcMicro) anonymises
  microdata for public- and scientific-use files and estimates
  disclosure risk.

Both produce data meant to be analysed in place of the original. masque
produces a development copy: analysts write code on it and the data
owner runs that code on the real data through the private recipe. It
keeps the experimental design (treatments, blocks, plots), and a
conditional clone (`conditional = TRUE`) also keeps the treatment means
of the outcome. Every column’s role and action is checked against a
fixed vocabulary before anything is masked.

## Documentation

Articles, in reading order:

1.  [Getting started with
    masque](https://max578.github.io/masque/articles/getting_started.html):
    the one-call path on a public fixture.
2.  [Recipe anatomy and the
    round-trip](https://max578.github.io/masque/articles/recipe_anatomy.html):
    what a recipe holds and how a pipeline built on the synthetic runs
    on the original.
3.  [Confidentiality and the threat
    model](https://max578.github.io/masque/articles/confidentiality.html):
    what a clone protects, the three modes, and the depth controls.
4.  [What a conditional clone keeps of the
    design](https://max578.github.io/masque/articles/design_preservation.html):
    eight classic field designs tested against one pass rule.

The [function
reference](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/index.html)
documents every exported function. Also on the site: [API stability
policy](https://max578.github.io/masque/API_STABILITY.html),
[changelog](https://max578.github.io/masque/news/index.html),
[contributing guide](https://max578.github.io/masque/CONTRIBUTING.html)
and [licence](https://max578.github.io/masque/LICENSE.html).

# Package index

## Guided masking

The main function, one call for a table, a folder, or a workbook.

- [`masque()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/masque.md) :
  Mask a dataset end to end with one guided call

## Role discovery

Inspect a data frame and decide what each column is and how to mask it.

- [`propose_roles()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/propose_roles.md)
  : Propose role and action classifications for the columns of a data
  frame
- [`set_role()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/set_role.md)
  : Set the role and action of one or more columns in a roles table
- [`role_options()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/role_options.md)
  : List every role and action combination masque accepts
- [`roles_validate()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/roles_validate.md)
  : Validate a roles table

## Cleaning input

Tidy names, labels and types before masking.

- [`clean_table()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/clean_table.md)
  : Tidy a dirty table's column names and category labels before masking
- [`conform_table()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/conform_table.md)
  : Bring a cleaned table to an analysable format, reporting every
  assumption

## Design detection

Identify environment scope and experimental design, then plot both to
check them.

- [`detect_design()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/detect_design.md)
  : Detect environment scope and experimental-design structure
- [`plot_design_summary()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/plot_design_summary.md)
  : Sanity-check visualisation for detected scope and design

## Masking

Make synthetic copies of one or many tables.

- [`mask()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/mask.md) : Make a
  synthetic copy of one table
- [`mask_set()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/mask_set.md)
  : Mask a multi-table set with cross-table-consistent aliasing
- [`read_set()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/read_set.md)
  : Read a set of tables from a folder, an Excel workbook, or a list
- [`write_set()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/write_set.md)
  : Write a masked set to disk, mirroring the input format
- [`synthetic()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/synthetic.md)
  : Extract the synthetic data from a masque object
- [`recipe()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/recipe.md) :
  Extract the recipe from a masque object
- [`roles()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/roles.md) : The
  role table of a masked clone
- [`data_card()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/data_card.md)
  : Write a data card for a masked clone

## Recipe round-trip

Persist a recipe and re-target a pipeline between original and
synthetic.

- [`save_recipe()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/save_recipe.md)
  : Save a masque recipe to disk
- [`read_recipe()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/read_recipe.md)
  : Read a masque recipe from disk
- [`apply_recipe()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/apply_recipe.md)
  : Translate a data frame into the synthetic namespace
- [`unmask()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/unmask.md) :
  Translate data from the synthetic namespace back to the original
- [`reveal_maps()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/reveal_maps.md)
  : Reveal the level maps held inside a recipe

## Leakage audit

Check a synthetic for residual structural leakage.

- [`audit_mask()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/audit_mask.md)
  : Audit a masque object for leakage and shareability risks

## Known-truth controls

Null, negative and positive control datasets derived from a table by a
declared spec.

- [`control_spec()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/control_spec.md)
  : Declare the controls to derive from a table
- [`controls()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/controls.md)
  : Derive null, negative and positive controls from a table
- [`control_table()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/control_table.md)
  : Produce one control dataset

## Plan and handover

Roles and named specs in one object, and what an analyst receives.

- [`masque_plan()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/masque_plan.md)
  : A masking plan: roles and named specs in one object
- [`clone_plan()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/clone_plan.md)
  : The plan in clone vocabulary, for the analyst
- [`save_plan()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/save_plan.md)
  [`read_plan()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/save_plan.md)
  : Save and read a masking plan as YAML
- [`handover()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/handover.md)
  : Hand a clone to an analyst

## Geospatial post-processing

Coarsen or re-anchor synthetic coordinates while keeping them on land
and plausible.

- [`jitter_coordinates()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/jitter_coordinates.md)
  : Coarsen geographic coordinates by an on-land privacy jitter
- [`synthesise_geospatial()`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/synthesise_geospatial.md)
  : Re-anchor synthetic geospatial coordinates at plausible-but-fake
  locations

## Package

- [`masque-package`](https://max578.github.io/masque/reference/masque-package.md)
  : masque: Synthetic Copies of Confidential Data Tables
